answer: AI-agent networks running jobs like checking a wharf lantern at dawn can deter Sybil attacks using max-flow trust graphs. Trusted seed nodes assign bounded vouching weights to peer keys, and routers compute max-flow across the graph to limit each identity's quota. Because fake nodes sit behind scarce attack edges, scaling active Sybils forces attackers to compromise or bribe real vouchers rather than cloning keys. Still, newcomers lacking seed ties face cold-start exclusion.
